title: Piaule Catskill Retreat
description: Set on ninety acres above the town of Catskill, Piaule is a landscape hotel of twenty four minimalist cabins, a spa, and a central lodge. Montana Contracting delivered the structures with a precision that lets the architecture recede into the surrounding forest.
Each cabin is a study in restraint. Floor to ceiling glass, warm timber, and concrete meet at tolerances measured in millimeters, so the building quiets down and the view becomes the room.
The work called for close coordination between our field teams and the design team: protecting mature trees, managing a sensitive grade, and finishing every surface to a gallery standard.

title: Hudson River House
description: A private residence perched to capture the full sweep of the Hudson. The house opens almost entirely to the water, with expanses of glass framed in blackened steel and stone drawn from the region.
Building on a steep riverfront grade meant engineering foundations and drainage with real care. Our team sequenced the work to keep the site stable through every season of construction.
Inside, the finish work is quiet and exact. Rift white oak, honed stone, and clean plaster carry through the living spaces without a visible seam.

title: Germantown Compound
description: Two homes, one family, one site. The first is an artist studio built for the daughter, a single-family residence where floor-to-ceiling glass pulls the wooded landscape indoors and every surface was finished to a gallery standard. The second is Meadow House, a 2,800-square-foot ground-up residence set within a gently sloping meadow, bordered to the south by dense forest.

Meadow House reinterprets the barn typology through a contemporary lens. Three distinct volumes pivot outward to create intimate covered inner courtyards, integrating indoor and outdoor living while preserving privacy. An entrance pavilion houses the garage, office, and workout area. A central living pavilion with a lofted ceiling opens southward to capture natural light and long forest views. A separate bedroom wing is set back into the landscape, creating a quieter, more secluded domain.

The approach is carefully choreographed. A curved brick wall defines the northern facade, concealing the scale of the home and guiding circulation along a meandering path. The moment of compression gives way to openness upon entry, where expansive south-facing glazing reveals the forest and meadow. An undulating roof plane with integrated solar panels unifies all three volumes, and a geothermal system heats and cools the highly efficient envelope. The orientation follows principles of feng shui, aligning the home to welcome light, warmth, and integration with the landscape.

title: Twisted Ridge
description: A sculptural residence set into a wooded ridge, its roofline twisting to follow the slope and open each room to a different piece of the valley.
The geometry was unforgiving. Every framing member met the next at a shifting angle, so we modeled the entire structure before a single board was cut.
The result is a home that feels carved from the site, with cantilevers and glass that make the woods part of the interior.

title: The Gym Englewood
description: A full reimagining of a fitness club, delivered in stages so the doors never closed. We rebuilt the floors, systems, and finishes around an operating business.
Staged work on a live site takes planning. We isolated construction from members, and turned over finished zones on a schedule the client could count on.
New training floors, group rooms, and locker rooms were finished in a clean, durable palette built to take heavy daily use for years.

title: Monte Nido West Nyack
description: A second Monte Nido facility, built inside a different estate on Sickletown Road in West Nyack. Same program, same standard, a different property with its own layout to solve around.

The scope covered a full conversion: bedrooms, a shared kitchen and dining room, a living room, and clinical space, all built into the existing envelope of a large residential home rather than a purpose-built facility.
Every room was finished to a residential standard, not an institutional one. Natural light, real materials, and a floor plan that supports both daily therapy and daily life.

title: Monte Nido New City
description: A residential treatment center built inside a converted estate in New City. The brief called for a clinical program to run inside a home that never feels clinical.

Bedrooms, group rooms, and therapy spaces sit alongside a working kitchen and dining room, each finished in the same warm, residential material palette. Circulation was planned around calm: wide hallways, natural light, and sightlines that never feel institutional.
The building reads as a home first. It has to, for the people who live and heal inside it.

title: Dairyland, Chef's Warehouse
description: A full-gut conversion of 26,000 square feet of raw industrial space into a considered, design-forward workplace. The building was stripped to its shell and rebuilt around a new organizational logic: open workspaces, private offices, and a showpiece test kitchen that anchors the floor plan.

The technical scope was deep. All-new mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems run through the structure. Helical piles were driven to stabilize the foundation on Bronx soil. A custom interior storefront system wrapped in decorative steel partitions the space while keeping sightlines open and light moving between zones.

The finishes tell the story. A state-of-the-art test kitchen with commercial-grade equipment. Local graffiti artists commissioned to bring original work onto the walls, giving the office a sense of place and texture that reads more gallery than corporate. High-end materials and tight tolerances throughout, executed off plans by GMA Architects of St. Louis.

title: Dunkin' Greenwood Lake
description: One lot, one road, one drive-thru that had to work. Dunkin' needed a ground-up store on a tight, high-visibility parcel on a main road in Greenwood Lake, with a full drive-thru lane fit into a site that left almost no margin for one.

The building and the drive-thru lane were planned together from the first site plan. The lane wraps close along the property line, clear of customer parking and the front entrance, with the menu board and canopy set to the grade break on that side of the lot. Stacked stone at the base and orange trim under the roofline carry the brand without crowding the site.

Inside, the counter, kitchen, and a full espresso and cold brew bar sit behind digital menu boards, finished in the dark ceiling and warm tile used across Dunkin' builds. Every utility tie-in, grading line, and curb cut was coordinated against the drive-thru lane before the foundation went in, so cars, customers, and staff move through the same tight site without crossing paths.

title: Dunkin' New City
description: Three weeks, start to finish. Dunkin' needed a full interior renovation of an operating store in New City, and the schedule left no room for a slow start or a second mobilization.

We ran the job with our own crews. Every one of our superintendents came up as a carpenter first, so the people running the schedule are the same people who can pick up a tool and close a gap in it. A three-week interior turn depends on a crew that can move from demo to rough-in to finish without waiting on outside labor to catch up.

The result is a full rebuild behind the same four walls. New counters, new digital menu boards, a full espresso and cold brew bar, dark tile and black ceiling throughout, and the branded wall signage that anchors the dining room. The store reopened on schedule, finished to the same standard as a ground-up build.

title: Palisades Mod Ranch
description: A 4,900-square-foot ranch in Palisades, New York, designed around two principles: open space and natural light. Fourteen-foot Marvin Contemporary Windows and Wasco skylights pull daylight deep into the plan, while ceiling heights shift from 12 to 18 feet to define each zone without walls.

The exterior is a composition of materials. Clear cedar and ipe siding sit alongside Cembonit fiber cement panels and natural stone veneer, all capped by a black standing-seam metal roof. The material palette feels grounded and modern at once, aging into the wooded Palisades site rather than fighting it.

Inside, every system was chosen for precision and comfort. Warmboard radiant heating runs underfoot. Three Stuv wood-burning fireplaces anchor the main living spaces. Liberamente kitchen cabinetry, a RadioRa lighting control system, and a fully-finished basement complete a home built to perform as well as it looks.

title: Tuxedo Residence
description: A transitional custom home set on a wooded lot in Tuxedo, built around long sightlines to the trees and a lake below. Arched windows and a two-story great room pull daylight deep into the plan.

The material palette runs light stucco and dark charcoal accent walls against warm hardwood floors, with brass and gold hardware carried through every room. A curved staircase and a coffered-ceiling foyer anchor the entry.

The kitchen centers on a black-and-white island with a marble top, flanked by a full wet bar finished in the same stone. Bathrooms throughout mix marble, stacked stone, and brass fixtures, each one built to its own material story.

title: Nyack Fresh Market
description: A full storefront and interior buildout for an independent grocer in downtown Nyack. The signature curved sign and awning needed to read from the street, and the interior needed to move a full grocery format through checkout without a bottleneck.

Four checkout lanes sit against a branded feature wall, with a customer service counter and full deli, produce, and hot food sections laid out behind it. Exposed ceiling and track lighting keep the industrial shell honest while the finishes stay warm.
The store opened as a full-service neighborhood market, built to move volume without losing the feel of a local shop.

title: Catskills Cabin
description: A modern cabin in the Catskills, built around a single open living, dining, and kitchen room under a vaulted ceiling. A wood-burning stove anchors the space between two runs of tall windows facing the tree line.

The kitchen runs dark cabinetry against a white island, paired with a natural wood dining table and a loft level tucked above. Every material choice leans toward warmth: wide-plank hardwood floors, leather seating, and tile finishes that read handmade rather than manufactured.
Bathrooms carry the same restraint, fluted tile and matte black or brushed nickel fixtures against a simple white tub. The whole house is built to disappear into the woods around it.

title: Catch Air Nanuet
description: A full buildout of an indoor family entertainment center in Nanuet, built around a space-themed play structure that had to hold up to daily use by kids.

Multi-level slides, climbing structures, and soft-play zones were built into an existing commercial shell, with exposed structural ceiling left as part of the design rather than covered over. Every surface, from the flooring graphics to the themed wall panels, was coordinated as one build.
The result is a durable, fully themed space designed to run at full capacity every day it is open.

title: 45 Haviland Court
description: A new custom home at 45 Haviland Court, with quiet bedrooms and a bathroom finished in terracotta subway tile, dark stone, and light cabinetry.
The new project photography follows the rooms from the primary suite to the vanity wall, where a full-width backlit mirror brings even light to the space.
